page: Amazon Web Services c3.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz and includes a 25 MB L3 cache. It supports Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX) and AES cryptography, though it lacks newer instruction sets like AVX-512 or AMX. The instance is equipped with 15.0 GB of system memory, yielding 1.88 GB per core, and includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is rated at a 1 Gbps baseline.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by bottom 25% ratings in stress-ng single-core and gzip compression, alongside a poor rating in Geekbench single-core tests. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and software compilation benchmarks placing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth remains average across both cached and uncached read/write operations. The local NVMe SSD storage supports average performance for static web serving and database operations, though Redis SET operations fall into the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3.2xlarge offers a balanced profile for legacy compute-intensive workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores and local NVMe storage without requiring modern instruction sets or high memory-to-vCPU ratios. Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, this instance is suited for multi-threaded batch processing, software compilation, static web serving, and basic database operations. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks, modern LLM inference, or memory-bound applications.
